title: San Diego County reminds CalFresh recipients of work requirements deadline in September
text:
San Diego County reminds CalFresh recipients of work requirements deadline in September
San Diego County officials announced on Sep. 16 that some CalFresh recipients could lose their benefits in October if they do not meet new federal work requirements. Since June, certain adults must complete at least 20 hours per week, or 80 hours per month, of work, volunteer service, or education activities to remain eligible for CalFresh.
Recipients are given three months of benefits at the start of their renewal period to allow time to connect with qualifying activities. Approximately 1,700 county residents are at risk of losing their benefits on Oct. 1 if they do not respond to the county by the end of September with proof that they met the requirements or qualify for an exemption.
If a recipient misses the deadline and loses benefits, they can reapply. To regain eligibility, individuals must complete 30 consecutive days of qualifying activities and will be reviewed annually thereafter. Activities that count toward meeting these requirements include employment as well as volunteering at food banks, schools, or places of worship. The county provides an optional volunteer hours form to assist with reporting.
County staff are available to help residents identify qualifying activities and connect them with job training and education opportunities. For assistance, residents can call the Access Customer Service Call Center at 1-866-262-9881 and are encouraged to keep contact information current online at BenefitsCal.com.
CalFresh is California’s version of the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), which provides nutritious food support for those in need. San Diego County Government delivers essential services through groups focused on public safety, health and human services, land use and environment, finance and general government, community services; supports historic preservation; manages regional airports; serves diverse regions including urban and rural areas; and is led by a Board of Supervisors providing legislative leadership, with Sarah Aghassi serving as interim chief administrative officer, according to the official website.
